description:
Event handlers in Filament components are registered via Filament.Hooks.register_event_handler/1. Their wire identity (the phx-click value sent to the browser) must be stable across re-renders — the same handler must produce the same string ref so LiveView can route click events correctly. This stability was historically provided by use_memo wrapping inside the dynamic fn. After T2 (hoisting), use_memo runs in the hoisted binding pass (before the struct) — this ticket verifies that stability is preserved and cleans up if anything was left behind.

READ FIRST:
- lib/filament/hooks.ex                  (register_event_handler/1 implementation)
- lib/filament/vnode_compiler.ex         (wrap_node_if_needed for register_event_handler — lines ~110-143)
- lib/filament/renderer.ex               (how hook slots are managed per fiber)
- lib/filament/reconciler.ex             (fiber lifecycle, hook slot numbering)
- examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_list.ex   (on_toggle / on_remove handlers)
- examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_item.ex   (on_click handlers)

HOW STABILITY WORKS TODAY:
register_event_handler(fn_literal) calls use_slot/1 which assigns a slot index to the
handler within the current fiber. The wire ref is "filament:<fiber_id>:<slot_index>".
Slot indices are assigned sequentially per render pass. As long as the same handler is
always the Nth hook slot call, it gets the same index and thus the same wire ref.

use_memo wraps fn literals so the same fn reference is returned for unchanged deps,
but the slot index assignment is what provides wire stability — not the fn identity.

WHAT TO VERIFY:
After T2, use_memo for event handlers runs in the hoisted binding pass:
  _d3 = register_event_handler(use_memo(fn -> fn_literal end, [dep1, dep2]))
This is equivalent to the old approach — use_memo still calls use_slot, slot index
is still assigned during the render pass, wire ref is still stable.

1. Write or run an existing test that:
   a. Renders a component with two event handlers (on_click / on_remove)
   b. Re-renders with changed props
   c. Asserts the wire refs (the phx-click attribute values) are identical across renders
   Check test/filament/ for existing handler stability tests. If none exist, add one.

2. In VNodeCompiler.wrap_node_if_needed for register_event_handler (lines ~118-143):
   Confirm the case still handles fn literals correctly in the hoisted context.
   The handler is now `_dN = register_event_handler(use_memo(fn -> fn_literal end, deps))`
   The use_memo runs before the %Rendered{} struct is built — confirm this is still
   within a live render call (it is, because hoisted bindings execute linearly in
   the render fn body).

3. If any use_memo calls remain INSIDE the dynamic fn closure (i.e., not hoisted),
   identify them and move them to the hoisted pass. After T2 this should not be
   the case, but verify by inspecting the generated AST for a template with handlers:
   ```elixir
   quote do IO.inspect(~F"""<button on_click={fn -> :ok end}>click</button>""") end
   ```
   Examine the output — dynamic fn should only contain variable refs, no use_memo calls.

4. Confirm there are no calls to use_slot (transitively via use_memo or direct) inside
   the dynamic fn closure in any generated template.

ACCEPTANCE:
- `mix test` passes including any new handler stability test
- Chrome: localhost:4000 — add two todos; toggle the first (on_click fires); verify
  the second todo's toggle still works after the first was toggled (slot indices stable)
- Chrome: remove a todo using the × button (on_remove fires); verify remaining todos
  and their handlers still work
- Chrome: add a new todo after removing one; verify all event handlers on all items work
  (this exercises re-render with changing list length — a common source of slot drift)
title: Verify event handler slot stability; retire use_memo from dynamic fn path
